core_obligations: Reduce to the strictly henselian case (proof lines 19173-19185): since base changes of smooth morphisms are smooth it suffices to prove local acyclicity; the property depends only on the ring map of strict henselisations, so one may replace f by its base change to Spec(O^sh_{S,s}) and assume S strictly henselian with s over the closed point.

Apply smooth base change (proof lines 19187-19206): for F = Z/nZ with n prime to the residue characteristic, smooth base change gives that f^{-1}R^qg_*F -> R^qh_*e^{-1}F is an isomorphism for the diagram formed with t; the stalk-form lemma then yields the middle equality in the displayed chain of cohomology groups over F_{x,t}, Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) x_S t, Spec(O^sh_{S,s}) x_S t and t, the outer equalities following from S = Spec(O^sh_{S,s}).

Conclude (proof lines 19207-19231): since t is the spectrum of a separably closed field, those cohomology groups are M in degree 0 and vanish otherwise, which is exactly local acyclicity of f at x relative to F, and hence universal local acyclicity.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a strictly henselian base with the closed point where the geometric point lives.
Use smooth base change and the stalk reformulation to identify the cohomology of the vanishing-cycle variety with that of the point t.
Read off the defining vanishing for local acyclicity.
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves that a smooth morphism is universally locally acyclic (statement lines 19166-19170). The proof (proof lines 19172-19231) reduces to a strictly henselian base using the dependence of local acyclicity on the ring map of strict henselisations, applies smooth base change for constants of invertible order, converts the base change statement into an equality of cohomology groups by the stalk-form lemma, and reads the defining vanishing off the separably closed residual field. H2: one reduction plus one base change computation, written out.
